component.name: Knowing Jesus Today
component.summary: Holy Bible and the Orthodox faith

description.p: Knowing Jesus Today is a Bible reader for Linux: read the Holy Bible with the Orthodox faith, study it with the Holy Fathers, and keep it all on your computer, to read also without the internet.

ul.li: The Holy Bible in many languages, with search, comparison, cross-references and the Greek and Hebrew words
The Holy Fathers beside every chapter, and their writings to read like books, by topic and by era
Bookmarks, colours, notes and Study Pads, kept in step with your phone and the website when you sign in
A library of free Bibles, commentaries, dictionaries and books from CrossWire and AndBible, the Septuagint and the Church Fathers first
The Bible Maps in the land's real colours, with story maps such as the journeys of St Paul
Today with God: the verse of the day, the feasts, the saints and the readings of the day
Share a verse as a picture, with your own photo if you like

description.p: Everything you choose to download is kept on your computer.

description.p: Sign in with your study key, as on the website (or with a name and password).

The Holy Fathers as on the website: read by topic, in coloured tiles (Prayer, Repentance, the Mother of God …); the Fathers in their eras, each era in its own colour, with the topics they wrote on; the topics of each writing; and a search.

My Study in two columns: the Study Pads on the left, the bookmarks and notes beside them, each scrolling on its own (drag the line between them to change their widths). Every page now fits medium and small windows: the small-screen layout follows the room the pages really have.
Choose several verses as on the website: click the first, then the last. “+ Next verse” and “− One less” now sit beside the verse reference. The last chosen verse is always fully highlighted.
The first click after opening the app or a chapter chooses one verse, instead of selecting half the page; the page no longer slides to the end of the text when you click into it.

A Library: the free Bibles, commentaries, dictionaries and books of CrossWire and AndBible, the Orthodox ones first (the Septuagint, St John Chrysostom, the Early Church Fathers, the Didache). You see the list first and choose; each is then read without the internet. A Bible from the Library becomes one of your Bibles; the commentaries show beside the Holy Fathers in the reader. A click always chooses one verse, even a shaky one. Study Pads in coloured cards, with their own colours and emoji, and their bookmarks highlighted in the pad's colour. The maps: the rest of the world (countries and today's capitals), a scale ruler, slower zoom, All places and Story maps as on the website. Side panels can be made wider or narrower by dragging their edge. Today with God can be shared as a picture or as text.

A new app icon. Choosing verses is steady: a click chooses one verse; Shift+click (or "Next verse too") makes a range; Ctrl+click adds one verse. Share a verse as a picture, as on the website: eight looks or your own photo from this computer, four shapes, three kinds of letters; copy it or save it. Study Pads show by their names, not as tags, and a new Study Pad is made with its own name. Edit a bookmark in one place: its colour, note and Study Pads. In My Study, fold the Study Pads and the bookmarks away, sort them (Bible order, newest, oldest, last changed, colour), rename a Study Pad, and edit each bookmark.

Like the website reader: tap a verse, then another, to choose everything between them (or choose "from verse … to verse" in the book picker), then bookmark, highlight or write a note on the whole range. Above each chapter: your notes and bookmarks in it (with Next), the people and places named in it, and the Holy Fathers on it. Notes show as one short line under their verse; click to read or edit the whole note.

Clearer bookmarks: the bar shows what a verse already has (bookmark, colour, note, Study Pads); remove a bookmark or its colour, edit or delete a note, and undo each change. Downloads in a queue, two at a time, each with its own progress, to stop or try again. Book names follow the language of the Bible being read. The app's language follows the computer unless chosen. The Orthodox cross drawn the right way.
Steadier: right click (or a long press) chooses the verse and shows the one action bar, now with words beside its icons; the maps use less memory; if the app ever freezes, a small log shows where.

A richer reader: it always opens on the Holy Bible and offers to continue at the very verse where you stopped; choose a book, a chapter and a verse; books coloured by their kind with a legend; right click (or a long press) on a verse for everything you can do with it; cross-references; the Greek and Hebrew words with their meanings; the words of Christ in red; your notes under their verses; the people and places of each chapter.
Faster, simpler and more modern: its own icons, smooth maps, pages that open at once, downloads four files at a time, and a layout that fits small screens and phones.
A new app, made for the computer: no web pages any more. Signing in to My KJT works in the app.
